Implement downscoped token exchange (subset of scopes, optionally restricted_to a file/folder) where least-privilege calls help

approval.cost: No listing fee, review fee, or API access fee is stated in the docs read; a free developer account is documented as sufficient to create and configure OAuth 2.0 apps
approval.trigger: No Box-operated review is required for end users to connect to your OAuth 2.0 app; user consent is the authorization, and no pre-approval user/install cap is documented for OAuth 2.0 user apps. The gates that do exist are per-customer enterprise-admin gates, not a Box marketplace review: (1) Server apps (JWT/CCG) 'must be authorized by a Box Admin before use' (automatic at creation on free developer accounts; in an enterprise the developer clicks Review and Submit on the Authorization tab, 'Your enterprise's Box Admin will receive an email to approve the application in the Admin Console', and the developer is emailed the approve/deny decision). (2) Unpublished OAuth 2.0 (user-auth) apps 'may require enablement by a Box Admin or Co-Admin' if they are inactive by default in that enterprise; submission via the Enablement tab emails the enterprise's Primary Admin, or an admin adds/enables the app by Client ID in Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps. (3) 'When an application's scopes or access level change, the application must be re-authorized for the changes to take effect' (automatic on free developer accounts; admin re-submission required in enterprises). One stated enterprise cap: 'When a new enterprise is created, it can authorize up to 10,000 custom apps.' Listing (optional): Box Integrations publishing runs Developer Console > My Platform Apps > Publishing tab > submission checklist > Submit for Approval; prerequisites include 'The platform app is in a finished state and ready for production usage' and 'The platform app leverages OAuth 2.0 authentication, as Integrations do not support any other authentication methods'. On timeline the docs say only: 'the Box Partner team will be notified and review your request as soon as possible'.
approval.wait: Not stated (admin approval and Integrations review have no stated durations; Integrations: 'as soon as possible')

blockers.detail: 'A Refresh Token is valid for 60 days and can be used to obtain a new Access Token and Refresh Token only once... Every time an application uses the Refresh Token to get a new Access Token the Refresh Token is invalidated and a new Refresh Token is returned with the new Access Token. This new Refresh Token is then again only valid for 1 use within 60 days.' If your app fails to persist the newest pair, the connection is dead and the user must re-authorize; tokens must be refreshed at least once every 60 days or the user goes through the full flow again.
blockers.howToClear: Persist the new refresh token atomically on every refresh and schedule refreshes well inside 60 days.
blockers.title: Single-use rotating refresh tokens

blockers.detail: The authentication method is set automatically for User apps and cannot be changed after app creation; a User (OAuth 2.0) app cannot later become a JWT/CCG server app or vice versa. You must create a new app.
blockers.howToClear: Decide User vs Server at creation; there is no conversion path.
blockers.title: App type/auth method is a one-way door

blockers.detail: Scopes are configured on the app in the Developer Console, not requested per-authorization; the consent screen reflects the console configuration, and changing scopes later triggers admin re-authorization in enterprise contexts.
blockers.howToClear: Finalize Application Scopes before enterprise customers enable the app.
blockers.title: Scopes live on the app, not the request

flavor.recommended: A Platform App (User type) using standard OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow ('User Authentication (OAuth 2.0)')
flavor.why: The object is a Platform App in the Box Developer Console. For user-delegated access you create it with app type User, which Box labels 'User Authentication (OAuth 2.0)'; the authentication method is set automatically and cannot be changed after app creation. Credentials are a Client ID and Client Secret on the app's Configuration tab. 'Because the token belongs to the person who signed in, your application reaches exactly the content that user owns or collaborates on, and any content it creates lives in that user's own account.' Users can belong to any Box enterprise (or a free account); no shared tenant is required. Scopes are configured on the app (Application Scopes, e.g. root_readonly 'Read all files and folders stored in Box', root_readwrite), and effective permission is 'the overlap between the user's own access and the scopes you enabled for the application, so a call can fail even when the user can see the file'. Box also supports downscoped tokens: exchanging a token for a narrower one (subset of scopes, optionally restricted_to a specific file/folder or shared link).

humanMust: Get Developer Console access (sign in with a Box enterprise account or sign up for a free developer account)
Create the User app and configure it (Application Scopes, OAuth 2.0 Redirect URI(s), CORS domains if browser-side JS will call the API); copy the Client ID / Client Secret
(Conditional, per enterprise customer) Submit the app for admin enablement via the Enablement tab, or hand the Client ID to an admin to enable it in Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps
(Optional) Publish to Box Integrations via the Publishing tab and Submit for Approval
name: Box
nuances: Content lands in different trees by auth method: OAuth 2.0 tokens write into the consenting user's own account; JWT/CCG tokens write into the Service Account's folder tree (root folder ID 0), invisible to users until shared. Mixing methods in one product causes 'missing file' confusion.

Redirect URIs: Box performs 'an exact match check'; scheme, domain, path, and query parameters must match a configured URI; URIs must be HTTPS, or HTTP only for localhost/loopback (which get port flexibility only); duplicate URIs are not permitted.

'When you explicitly revoke a developer token for a given app via the Developer console, all webhooks created by that application get deleted.' Box also warns that server-side Web App Integrations configuration 'is no longer supported' (existing ones keep working but can't be modified), and public availability now runs through Box Integrations listing, which requires OAuth 2.0 (JWT/CCG apps cannot be listed as Integrations).
Access tokens are valid 60 minutes across all auth methods, including the Developer Token; a refresh can be performed before or after the access token expires.
prerequisites: Developer Console access (Box enterprise account or free developer account)
Redirect URI(s) registered exactly (HTTPS, or HTTP localhost/loopback)
A token store that persists the newest refresh token on every refresh

steps.detail: Sign in to the Developer Console (Box enterprise account or free developer account). New App > choose User app type > Create; authentication is automatically OAuth 2.0.
steps.title: Create a User app in the Developer Console

steps.detail: On the Configuration tab: set Application Scopes; add OAuth 2.0 Redirect URI(s) (exact match; HTTPS, or HTTP only for localhost/loopback); add CORS domains if browser-side JS will call the API (skip if server-side only); copy the Client ID / Client Secret.
steps.title: Configure scopes, redirect URIs, CORS

steps.detail: If the app will operate inside a Box enterprise where unpublished user-auth apps are inactive by default, submit via the Enablement tab (emails the enterprise's Primary Admin), or hand the Client ID to an admin to add/enable it in Admin Console > Platform > Platform Apps. (JWT/CCG server apps always require this admin authorization in an enterprise.)
steps.title: (Conditional) Get enterprise admin enablement

steps.detail: Build the authorization URL from the Client ID and a registered redirect URI and send the user to Box; the user logs in and approves the application's scopes. Box redirects back with a short-lived authorization code; exchange it at POST api.box.com/oauth2/token (grant_type=authorization_code) with your client secret for an access token + refresh token pair; store both per user.
steps.title: Run the authorization flow

steps.detail: Call the API with Authorization: Bearer (access tokens valid 60 minutes). Refresh before the 60-day refresh-token window closes and store the NEW refresh token every time (each refresh invalidates the presented one). If 60 days pass without a refresh, send the user through authorization again.
steps.title: Call the API; refresh (single-use rotation)

steps.detail: My Platform Apps > Publishing tab: complete the submission checklist (finished, production-ready app; OAuth 2.0 required), provide categories, descriptions, the 'Add' button URL, screenshots, an app icon, and support information, then Submit for Approval. 'The Box Partner team will be notified and review your request as soon as possible.'
steps.title: (Optional) Publish to Box Integrations

tagline: Standard OAuth 2.0 with no Box-side review for user connections: the friction is enterprise admin enablement for unpublished apps, scopes fixed on the app rather than the request, and refresh tokens that are single-use and die after 60 days without a refresh.

time.active: ~15 min of console setup + ~1-2 hrs of flow code
